pass_a_gloss:
It is written, 'Do not despise one of these little ones, because their angels always see the face of the Father.' Then how will we not be accused by the holy angels, as if we are neglecting the weaknesses of our brethren and not rather making every effort to support their weakness, being conscious of it. I do not want you to be ignorant, brethren, that our fathers were all under the cloud. Paul, having commanded not to eat things sacrificed to idols to those who seem to have perfect knowledge, tries to persuade from the things that happened to the ancients that the matter is not beneficial but rather dangerous, and that it is not without harm for those who are accustomed to do wrong to attack. For it brings about doing what is not lawful, as the human mind is easily led astray to what is not proper. Therefore, it receives not a beautiful image of the matter, but rather a very similar one, the things that happened to the Israelites who came from blood in the wilderness. And it shows very clearly that wanting to live with the unfaithful would not be without harm even to those who are deserted. What he says is that those who were freed from slavery were perfected through the cloud in the sea, with the cloud suspended in the middle, with Moses mediating, and they ate the bread from heaven and drank the life-giving drink. For Christ himself, being the rock, nourished them, and although he suffered death voluntarily, he is unbroken as God. And we say that such things are prefigurations of spiritual matters.

And what happened to the elders? They were corrupted in Sattin, they served idols, they were devoted to Beelphagor. The ones baptized in the cloud and in the sea, although they ate the bread from heaven and drank the spiritual drink, they clashed with the idolaters. Since they were fellow diners and touched the idolatrous table, they easily fell into apostasy and danced with women, as the prophet said. For this is what it means to rise up to play. It is dangerous to associate with the wicked and faithless. Solomon said, 'The one who walks with the wise will be wise, but the one who walks with the foolish will be known.' We too, before our faith in Christ, were yoked to the demons' greed and served the spiritual Pharaoh, that is, Satan. We vainly gave him honor, like clay and brick, being occupied with the works of the flesh. But the mediator between God and men, Christ Jesus, gave himself as a ransom for all and led us through the turbulent sea of this life, perfecting us through holy baptism. He is the cloud from above and the spiritual cloud, providing living water to those who love him. The living water is the Spirit.

And Christ said, 'He who believes in me, as the Scripture said, rivers of living water will flow from his belly,' and the divine evangelist, explaining what was said, immediately added to the words about this, 'But this he said about the Spirit which those who believe in him were about to receive;' and we have eaten the truly life-giving bread, we drink the spiritual drink, just as they also drank the water from the rock; and the rock was Christ, who is also for us
pass_b_english: We are warned not to despise any of the little ones, for their angels always behold the face of the Father, and if we neglect the weaknesses of our brethren, we will be accused by the holy angels, as if we are neglecting their weaknesses and not rather making every effort to support their weakness, being conscious of it.

Our fathers were all under the cloud, and Paul teaches us that eating things sacrificed to idols is not beneficial but rather dangerous, and that it is not without harm for those who are accustomed to do wrong to attack, for it brings about doing what is not lawful, as the human mind is easily led astray to what is not proper, and it receives not a beautiful image of the matter, but rather a very similar one, the things that happened to the Israelites who came from blood in the wilderness, as it is written (1 Corinthians 10:1-5).

The Israelites were perfected through the cloud in the sea, with Moses mediating, and they ate the bread from heaven and drank the life-giving drink, for Christ himself, being the rock, nourished them, and although he suffered death voluntarily, he is unbroken as God, and we say that such things are prefigurations of spiritual matters.

The elders were corrupted in Sattin, where they served idols and were devoted to Beelphagor, and this corruption led to a clash with the idolaters, despite the fact that they had been baptized in the cloud and in the sea, and had eaten the bread from heaven and drunk the spiritual drink, and they were corrupted, having become mixed with the idolaters, and having fallen into apostasy, as they fellowshipped and shared in the idolatrous table, they easily fell into apostasy and danced with women, as the prophet had warned (Numbers 25:1-3).

Solomon's words are relevant here: 'The one who walks with the wise will be wise, but the one who walks with the foolish will be known' (Proverbs 13:20), and we too, before our faith in Christ, were yoked to the demons' greed and served the spiritual Pharaoh, that is, Satan, and we vainly gave him honor, like clay and brick, being occupied with the works of the flesh, and being led astray, exchanging the truth for a lie.

But Christ Jesus, the mediator between God and men, gave himself as a ransom for all, and led us through the turbulent sea of this life, perfecting us through holy baptism, and he is the cloud from above, providing living water to those who love him, and this living water is the Spirit, as Christ himself said, 'He who believes in me, as the Scripture has said, will have rivers of living water flowing from his heart' (John 7:38), and the evangelist explains that this refers to the Spirit that believers would soon receive.

We, too, have partaken of the truly life-giving bread and have drunk the spiritual drink, just as the Israelites drank water from the rock in the wilderness, and the rock was Christ, who is our source of spiritual nourishment, and we have been led through the sea of this life, and have been perfected through holy baptism.
